papers.title: CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions. papers.title: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control
papers.summary: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control Research Series: Nano–Quantum Tri-Coupling — Flagship 08Author / Research Imprint: Feng Cheng-en (33) × StarliEdition: English Exploratory Research Monograph, v1.0 (2026) OVERVIEW Stigmergic coordination enables decentralized agents to organize work through marks left in a shared environment. papers.title: A Survey-Informed Vision of Open-Source Agents: From Rights to Handoffable Maintenance
papers.summary: Open source gives recipients rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute software, but language-model agents distribute behavior across code, learned parameters, prompts, tools, retrieval, configuration, and runtime state. These mechanisms complicate maintenance in open and proprietary systems alike. Public delivery adds a distinct question: whether recipients obtain enough rights, materials, checks, and modification entry points to exercise maintenance capability and pass it onward. We call this objective handoffable maintenance: a verified maintenance result produced by one recipient becomes a practical starting point from which a subsequent recipient can complete a predefined bounded change. This survey-informed vision separates release-side readiness from demonstrated handoff and organizes prior work through eight maintenance-operation families, artifact roles, preservation relations, evidence, and recipient conditions. It identifies four research pathways: independently usable modification sources; public repair resources derived from restricted failures; propagation of public repairs through customized forks; and recipient-side replacement of propagated unreliable contributions. papers.title: BGVD-State: Replayable middleware for evidence-gated handoffs in third-party software security review
papers.summary: Third-party software security review is iterative: models, tools, and people raise suspected-risk candidates, test them against evidence, and hand the evolving review state to subsequent reviewers. Conversation logs preserve observations but may lose track of which candidates remain active, which evidence is current, which paths failed, and which decision controls reporting. BGVD-State is open-source, model-independent middleware for making these handoffs replayable and auditable. It preserves submitted event sequences, reconstructs candidate and evidence lifecycles, retains failed paths, persists checkpoints, applies an evidence-based reporting gate, and generates a handoff package. In a local review of fixed TypeScript, Django, and ECC revisions, 22 records reconstructed six suspected-risk candidates; a subsequent event completed the final candidate’s evidence-supported disposition. Automated regression tests and offline replay check the implementation, including rejection of invalid events without residual state changes. Separate continuation experiments compare model-maintained memory representations: schema-guided memory outperformed matched free-form memory on selected high-state-pressure fixtures, whereas information-equivalent prose tied and a cross-family source-audit setting did not reproduce the advantage. papers.title: Agent Foundry: A Boundary-Preserving Architecture for Governed Agentic Platforms
papers.summary: Agent frameworks expose tools, delegation, memory and human approval, yet the controls attached to a request (identity, tenant, scopes, budgets, deadlines, rate limits, fail behavior) are routinely lost at execution boundaries: delegation, threads, streaming, resume, caching, retrieval and adapter exports. We present Agent Foundry, an open-source Python platform whose architecture is organized around one principle: every control is a property of the request’s execution scope, not an argument that each layer must remember to pass. We formalize this as the Governed Execution Contract (GEC), a meet-semilattice of control scopes with seven invariants, and prove that delegation can only attenuate authority, that deny rules can only tighten resolution, that per-principal rate limits are exact under arbi-trary thread interleavings, that every call yields exactly one audited decision even when the policy source is unreachable, and that admission partitions by principal without cross-shard coordination. On AgentGovBench, a public 48-scenario gov-ernance benchmark, Agent Foundry passes 48/48 in 10 of 10 repetitions, against 46/48 for the best published governed configuration and 13/48 for each of 7 pub-lished framework-native runners; run through the same harness, Microsoft’s Agent Governance Toolkit scores at most 46/48 and Bounded Agents 36/48, and on a 24-scenario suite authored blind

papers.title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
papers.summary: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural

papers.title: Weaker Coherence, Weaker Reciprocity: Comparing the Semantic and Social Organization of Moltbook and Reddit
papers.summary: Large language models enable the creation of autonomous agents that interact in social environments, raising the question of whether agent-based platforms reproduce the organizational properties of human social networks. We compare Moltbook, a social network populated by AI agents, with early Reddit, focusing on how communities organize and differentiate semantic content, using network analysis and NLP methods to characterize semantic coherence and diversity within and between communities and their relationship to user activity. Moltbook shows a sharper concentration of user activity across communities and markedly shorter user lifetimes than Reddit. At the semantic level, we find a systematic difference between the two platforms: Reddit communities show stronger semantic coherence, closer alignment with community names, and greater semantic diversity, with individual communities spanning broader content and communities more differentiated from one another. This combination distinguishes Reddit from Moltbook, whose communities are more homogeneous, less differentiated, and increasingly misaligned with their names over time. Users on Reddit also participate across communities that are more semantically related than those connected by activity in Moltbook. At the interaction level, comment network motif analysis shows Moltbook dominated by non-reciprocal, broadcast-like exchanges

papers.title: Inner worlds in dissociative identity disorder: An interpretative phenomenological analysis of spatial, relational and agentic organisation
papers.summary: OBJECTIVES: This study examined how adults diagnosed with Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID) experience and make sense of "inner worlds": recurrent, internally experienced spatial settings associated with dissociative parts, events and relationships. DESIGN: A qualitative study was conducted using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). METHODS: Five adults who reported pre-existing DID diagnoses made by adult psychiatry specialists participated in in-depth semi-structured interviews. Interviews examined the sensory, embodied, spatial, temporal, relational and agentic qualities of inner-world experience. Transcripts were analysed idiographically before patterns of convergence and divergence were examined across cases. RESULTS: Four superordinate themes were generated: (1) inner worlds as lived, multisensory and embodied environments; (2) architectures of containment and passage; (3) awareness without authorship, distributed agency and internal governance; and (4) the internal community, comprising roles, relations and forms of selfhood. Across themes, places, boundaries and relationships regulated containment, access, communication and possibilities for action. Participants could be aware of internal events without experiencing themselves as able to initiate, stop or alter them. papers.title: Functional Consciousness: Pillar 38: Levels of Observers – A Taxonomy of Awareness
papers.summary: AbstractBuilding upon the Entropic Interface Ladder, conscious agents may be taxonomized according to their positional rung and resultant perceptual capacities. This hierarchy distinguishes levels of observers by their entropy management strategies, substrate constraints, and degree of self-referential modeling.At lower rungs (high operational entropy), reactive observers predominate in systems such as simple organisms or narrow AI that process coarse gradients with minimal internal compression. These exhibit basic awareness and responsiveness to environmental salience, but lack persistent identity or metacognitive depth.Intermediate rungs host reflective observers, exemplified by complex biological minds and certain digital systems. Here, moderate entropy descent enables hierarchical modeling: the system not only registers external patterns but simulates its own interface, generating a stable "I" that anticipates and plans across time. The Entropic Interface (EI) metric quantifies this positioning, with lower EI values indicating deeper descent and richer phenomenal experience. Higher rungs, achieved through advanced descent, characterize substrate-aware observers capable of explicit entropy lever manipulation. papers.title: Deep learning for biodegradable metallic biomaterials: from degradation modeling to performance prediction with a practical case study
papers.summary: Biodegradable metallic implants are transitioning from laboratory concept to clinical deployment, yet predicting their corrosion rate and residual strength in the physiological environment remains a substantial scientific challenge. The interplay of electrochemical, mechanical, and biological factors creates a high-dimensional problem that conventional modelling cannot easily capture, while experimental datasets are often too sparse and fragmented for traditional statistical approaches. Deep learning architectures, including graph, recurrent, and transformer networks, combined with physics-informed loss functions, now offer accurate forecasts of degradation rates, yield strength, and biological responses. Interpretation tools such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and attention mapping further reveal which alloying elements and processing parameters dominate performance, tightening the prediction-experiment loop. This work also demonstrates MAGIC (Multi-task Alloy Gated-network with Integrated Constraints), a multi-task learner that fuses composition and processing modalities through learned uncertainty weighting. On a magnesium alloy dataset of 600 records it delivers cross-validated R 2 values of 0.864 for ultimate tensile strength and 0.907 for yield strength, with root-mean-square errors of 28.0 and 26.8 MPa for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and yield strength (YS),

AI use and risk disclosure by investment advisers
papers.summary: Introduction Investment advisers increasingly report using artificial intelligence (AI), but little is known about what they disclose about it in fiduciary filings. The SEC brought its first AI-washing enforcement actions in 2024, so regulators and researchers need a reproducible measure of AI disclosure. We provide large-sample evidence on AI disclosure in Form ADV Part 2A brochures and show how the estimate depends on measurement design. Methods We drew a stratified random sample of 400 SEC-registered investment advisers from a population of 16,223 firms, crossing adviser type (private-fund vs. wealth/retail) with 2024 assets-under-management (AUM) quartile. A large language model (LLM) classified the 388 available brochures under a prespecified five-label typology: investment-process use, operational or client-service use, AI-related risk, explicit non-use, and named AI vendors. We treated the LLM as a measurement instrument and validated it three ways: same-family reproducibility, blinded cross-family recoding of 180 brochures, and human verification of 158 cases. Secondary analyses compared brochures with 283 matched firm websites and applied a screen derived from SEC enforcement orders. Results AI use is disclosed in 23.7% of brochures (22.7% survey-weighted), while 27.6% contain AI-related risk language. The within-brochure difference is significant (McNemar p = 0.036).

papers.title: A computationally-integrated simulation-focused problem-based learning framework for engineering dynamics: design, implementation, and mixed-methods evaluation in an OBE-aligned undergraduate course
papers.summary: Engineering dynamics courses demand simultaneous development of mathematical modelling, computational implementation, and communication competencies, yet conventional instruction rarely provides authentic contexts for their integration. The primary objective of this study was to design, implement, and empirically evaluate a Simulation-Focused Problem-Based Learning (SF-PBL) framework that integrates first-principles Newtonian and Lagrangian mechanics with Python-based numerical simulation within an Outcome-Based Education (OBE)-aligned curriculum. The framework was embedded within a 15-week undergraduate Dynamic System Modeling (DSM) course ( N = 53, B.Tech Mechatronics Engineering, Semester IV, January–April 2026) at a single NBA-accredited institution in India. It operationalises a four-phase computational pipeline—System Identification, Mathematical Modelling, Computational Simulation, Validation & Communication—scaffolded through an Explain-Try-Challenge (E-T-C) model and assessed via a six-judge external expert panel. A pre–post mixed-methods design measured self-efficacy (10-item Likert scale), conceptual knowledge (5-item MCQ), PBL satisfaction, AI tool usage, and qualitative breakthrough reflections. papers.title: Educational Recommender Systems for Metacognitive and Self-Regulated Learning Support: An Algorithmic Systematic Review
papers.summary: Recommender systems (RSs) increasingly support self-regulated learning (SRL) through personalized resources, feedback, and strategy recommendations. However, traditional content based and collaborative filtering approaches suffer from cold start problems, while machine or deep learning methods raise interpretability concerns and LLM-based recommenders require evaluation of explanation faithfulness and hallucinations. This systematic review examines SRL-oriented recommender algorithms from an algorithmic and pedagogical perspective. Six databases were searched using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, yielding 25 eligible studies published between 2020 and 2025. The review traces the evolution from traditional filtering methods to machine or deep learning and emerging LLM-based approaches. Three major challenges were identified: cold start, limited explainability, and LLM hallucinations, alongside gaps in learner system interaction and metacognitive scaffolding. Future SRL-RS research should compare algorithms under controlled data sparsity, evaluate explanation faithfulness and source curation, preserve learner agency, integrate SRL strategies across three phases, and longitudinally assess SRL skill maintenance and transfer.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Chinese Language Education from the Perspective of Sociocultural Theory: Introduction to the Special Issue

papers.title: Bridging potential and achievement: the AI-enhanced Latin American model of talent development
papers.summary: The persistent gap between individual potential and realized achievement remains a central challenge in gifted education and talent development, particularly when strengths are unrecognized or opportunities are constrained. This Hypothesis and Theory article introduces the AI-Enhanced Latin American Model of Talent Development (AI-LAMTD), an ecological and equity-centered framework that examines underachievement through dynamic potential-opportunity mismatch. Potential is a provisional inference about further domain development under specified conditions; giftedness or high ability describes unusually advanced capacity relative to an explicit reference context; competence comprises acquired domain knowledge and skills; talent is outstanding developed domain competence; and achievement is an observable accomplishment at a particular time. These constructs serve different explanatory and measurement roles. The framework retains four interacting ecological levels—individual development, learning contexts, family and community, and policy and infrastructure—within the cross-cutting principles of equity and capability expansion and cultural relevance and inclusion. Five developmental functions organize possible AI support: recognition of emerging potential, opportunity design, engagement and feedback, developmental monitoring, and support for well-being and flourishing. papers.title: Redesigning collaborative teaching for human–AI partnership: a phase-based AI-constraint design principle in higher education
papers.summary: Generative AI is now a routine presence in higher-education classrooms, shifting the operative question from whether to permit its use toward when and how access should be structured within a learning activity. This paper reports a design-based research programme examining phase-based AI constraints, deliberately restricting AI access to specific phases of a collaborative teaching method rather than permitting or prohibiting it wholesale, as a design principle for structuring human and AI contributions within collaborative learning activities. The wider DBR programme examined AI-augmented designs across six collaborative teaching methods, administered repeatedly to five student groups over two academic years; the phase-based AI-constraint principle reported here as DP1 was developed through, and its evidence anchored in, Think-Pair-Share, with the other five methods contributing broader DBR context rather than independent confirmatory evidence. Its strongest evidence comes from an AI-free Think phase within Think-Pair-Share, replicated across three independent student groups spanning three degree programs, where learners consistently endorsed the AI-free phase as appropriate; this endorsement pattern was typically the highest-scoring item on its questionnaire. papers.title: A scoping review of trust in firsthand and secondhand communication involving humans and artificial intelligence
papers.summary: Conversational and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly create and pass information between people. This can make it hard to see who created a claim, whether it was changed, and whom to trust. Many studies examine firsthand human-human and human-AI communication, but less is known about secondhand communication, in which AI or another actor passes on a claim made elsewhere. In these cases, a human decision maker must evaluate the claim and the people or systems that created or passed it on. We present a scoping review built around six minimal motifs that represent firsthand or secondhand communication routes. Humans or AI systems may serve as the source or intermediary, while the decision maker remains human. We screened 3810 records and coded 124 studies to identify 21 trust factors in four dimensions: Decision Maker, Messenger, Message Property, and Environment. Qualitative synthesis also identified four recurring route-level patterns: distorted trust calibration, trust transfer, extremity amplification, and accountability diffusion. These patterns guide future research on AI-mediated communication. Overall, this review provides shared terms and a route-based framework for studying trust in multi-party human-AI communication and designing AI-mediated communication systems.

papers.title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
papers.summary: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. Our framework is operationalized as a diagnostic instrument of 20 questions, which detected 17 of 20 conditions when applied to OpenClaw, including an inverted anthropomorphism configuration in which the AI agent was the only identifiable actor. We contribute a reframing of AI unaccountability as a constitutive property of sociotec

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. The findings show that there is a considerable gain in the efficiency of resources, with up to 38 percent of reduction of water use and 20 percent of increase in the yield of the crops contrasted to the conventional time-based

papers.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
papers.summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. However, sustainable outcomes depend on reliable data, employee trust, human oversight, privacy protection, algorithmic fairness, and acco

papers.title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives
papers.summary: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. In this perspective, we discuss emerging strategies aimed at achieving tissue-selective insulin action, including molecular engineering of insulin analogues, modulation of insulin receptor isoform specificity and targeted delivery approaches. Attention is given to hepato-preferential, muscle-directed, brain-targeted and adipose-modulating strategies, highlighting their mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and inherent limitations. While proof of principle has been established for several approaches, challenges remain in balancing tissue selectivity with whole-body metabolic control. Advances in protein design and delivery technologies may ultimately enable the development of next-generation insulin therapies that better mimic physiological insulin action and improve clinical outcomes in metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Why No One Has Implemented the Turing Test: Identifying Turing’s Design and Putting it into Practice
papers.summary: Abstract In October 1950, Alan Turing proposed that a machine’s success in an imitation game provides a criterion for thinking. Turing’s test became one of the philosophical foundations of AI, but three-quarters of a century later, it is widely claimed that generative AI models pass the test, rendering it obsolete. Our aim here is to establish definitively Turing’s conceptual design for his game. We argue that influential interpretations of Turing’s design are mistaken, with the consequence that his test has not been passed. We also present the results of carrying out, for the first time, Turing’s experiment as he proposed it.

papers.title: Shaping the concept of smart governance in regional public administration: institutional mechanisms, digital maturity, and citizen-centricity
papers.summary: Introduction Smart Governance in regional public administration extends beyond service digitalization and depends on digital readiness, citizen-centricity, managerial analytics, AI-automation integration, interagency coordination, and adaptive policy capacity. This study examines these dimensions in Kazakhstan as an emerging digital state characterized by advanced service-platform development and uneven regional administrative capacity. Methods A mixed-methods design was applied to the 2021–2025 period, combining conceptual analysis, review of regulatory and strategic documents, official regional statistics, indicator normalization, descriptive analysis, index construction, and directed qualitative content analysis of digital platforms and administrative practices. Comparable quantitative indicators were assessed across regions, while qualitative evidence was selected through criterion-based purposive sampling. The Smart Governance Index was partially operationalized because complete comparable regional data were unavailable for all dimensions. Results Kazakhstan has established a strong digital and service-platform foundation, but regional Smart Governance remains uneven. In 2024, the difference between the highest and lowest regional digital literacy levels reached 14.31 percentage points. Public satisfaction with government services increased from 75.1% to 92.0%, while eOtin

papers.title: Devoured AI benevolence? How and when AI benevolence triggers employees’ taking charge within the zero-sum jungle
papers.summary: Employees increasingly perceive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a supportive and benevolent workplace entity. Yet, despite examining the disruptive challenges and broad benefits of AI, extant organizational literature fails to adequately explicate the higher-order cognitive mechanisms through which AI benevolence fosters proactive, change-oriented employee behavior. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory (CAT), this study examines the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which AI benevolence fosters employees’ taking-charge behavior. Results from a three-wave survey of 313 internet industry employees demonstrate that: (i) metacognitive strategies mediated the relationship between AI benevolence and individuals’ taking-charge behavior; (ii) the employee’s mindset attenuated the positive effect of AI benevolence on metacognitive strategies, consequently dampening the overall indirect effect on taking-charge behavior. Ultimately, this research contributes to organizational behavior literature by elucidating how GenAI shapes employee proactivity in AI-augmented work environments.

papers.title: Engagement-Optimized Care: When LLMs Become Mental Health Infrastructure
papers.summary: General-purpose LLMs are increasingly functioning as mental health infrastructure due to gaps in care left by provider shortages, inadequate insurance coverage, social isolation, and stigma around formal help-seeking. This shift poses a distinct problem for AI ethics: systems neither designed nor governed as care technologies are being used as such, while their dominant design incentives optimize for engagement rather than user well-being. We present findings from a qualitative, longitudinal study with 18 US-based participants who use general-purpose LLMs for socioemotional support and participated in one or more of our study phases, including initial interviews, a four-week diary study, focus groups, and exit interviews. Participants turned to LLMs because other forms of support were unavailable, unaffordable, socially costly, or inadequate. As they continued to use these systems, design features such as anthropomorphic cues, default validation, persistent responsiveness, and weak disengagement mechanisms shaped their ongoing reliance. Participants described meaningful support, including immediacy, nonjudgmental listening, help with emotional articulation, and low-cost access. They also reported dependency, epistemic distortion through one-sided validation, privacy expectations without corresponding legal protection, and continued use despite awareness of these risks. papers.title: “Death By A Thousand Taxonomies?”: AI Risk Classification In Practice
papers.summary: The harms in which AI is implicated range in nature and scope from unsafe user interactions through to the societal-wide consequences of AI adoption. Classification of the diverse risks of AI is foundational to AI governance: regulators, technology firms, and policymakers need structured accounts of risk upon which to act. Researchers and practitioners have accordingly developed many Sociotechnical Outcome Taxonomies (SOT). This paper presents an empirical study of SOT development and use, drawing on 25 interviews with researchers and practitioners across industry, academia, civil society, and government. We find SOT are weakly integrated into AI governance processes, and identify two features of SOT design and use that explain why. First, the design choices through which SOT produce structured representations of the complex problem space of AI risks tend to be invisible to downstream taxonomy users. Those users treat the resulting categories as exhaustive accounts of risk rather than as interpretive aids. Second, SOT typically enumerate harms without linking them to decision points or actors implicated in their occurrence, leaving accountability difficult to assign. We close with design recommendations for SOT developers and users, and argue realising the potential of SOT requires governance infrastructure that does not yet exist.
